newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares smash ceilings to 8th record close.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares smash ceilings to 8th record close.

text.p: Share prices in the Caracas Stock Exchange general index burst through technical ceilings to an eighth consecutive record high in heavy trade as foreign investors continued to flock to the market, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 5.36 percent to 9,273.38, its highest-ever close and first above the 9,000.00 point barrier.
A total of 34 stocks closed higher, four lower and five unchanged in trade of 16.011 billion bolivars ($33 million).
The sustained and sharp rally in share prices was sustained largely by foreign investors betting on Venezuela's economic recovery starting to swing into action, brokers said.

But many warned that the market was now in danger of becoming overheated and that sharp falls on profit-taking were imminent. "The rally will last as long as there is foreign investment. As soon as they stop buying and settle down the market will fall," said Rafael Alcantara, president of the Cavelba brokerage. Monday's trade was led by bellwether Electricidad de Caracas which continued strong gains to close up 54.95 bolivars at 779.95 bolivars.

A tariff hike approval equivalent to 75 percent over six months had boosted Electricidad beyond the market's already bullish tendency, with Merinvest President Augustin Cangas forecasting its stock could reach 1,000.00 bolivars on the rate rise.

Among other leading stocks, telephone company CANTV rose 35.00 bolivars to 3,035.00 bolivars while cement company Vencemos class 1 stock rose 10.00 bolivars to 1,650.00 bolivars and class 2 stock rose 6.00 bolivars to 1,570.00 bolivars.
